articles.title: Construction begins on our new Etsuda plant
articles.excerpt: Ground is broken on a purpose-built plant that adds production lines, a larger quality lab and room for the products our partners ask for next.
articles.coverAlt: Aerial rendering of the new Etsuda plant
articles.body:
This month we broke ground on our new plant in Etsuda. It is the biggest investment in Kawada's history, and it starts from a simple question our partners keep asking: *can you make more of this, and can you make the next thing too?*

The new site is planned to open in 2027. Here is what it will add, and what it means for the brands we already work with.

## More lines, shorter lead times

The plant is designed around additional high-speed lines for pads, liners and period pants. More capacity means we can schedule launches and seasonal peaks without pushing back existing orders.

- Dedicated lines for the Cotton Series and the Performance Series
- A separate line for period pants and maternity products
- Space reserved for lines we have not specified yet

<PullQuote cite="Kawada operations team">
We designed the building around the products our partners will ask for in five years, not only the ones they order today.
</PullQuote>

## A bigger quality lab

Every batch we ship is tested before it leaves the factory. The new lab doubles the bench space for absorbency, leakage and adhesion tests, and adds a room for material incoming inspection, so raw materials are checked before they ever reach a line.

<Figure
  src="/images/home/factory-lab.jpg"
  alt="A quality technician measuring a pad sample in the lab"
  caption="Batch testing will move into a larger lab with a dedicated incoming-materials room."
/>

## Built for lower impact

The plant is being built with energy-efficient lines, heat recovery and better waste sorting, so offcuts and packaging waste can be recycled rather than landfilled. We will share the numbers once the site is running.

## What happens to existing orders

Nothing changes. Our current factory keeps running at full capacity through construction, and we will move production in stages so no partner sees a gap in supply.

### Timeline

1. Groundwork and foundations: autumn 2026
2. Building shell and utilities: 2027
3. First lines commissioned and qualified: 2027

If you are planning a launch for 2027 or later and want to reserve capacity, [get in touch](/en/contact-us/) and we will walk you through the schedule.

articles.title: Meet Kawada at Cosmoprof Asia 2026 in Hong Kong
articles.excerpt: We are bringing the Cotton Series, the new overnight pad and our packaging options to Hong Kong this November. Book a meeting with our team.
articles.coverAlt: The Kawada team reviewing product samples and packaging
articles.body:
We are exhibiting at Cosmoprof Asia in Hong Kong this November, and we would love to meet you there.

## What you can see on the stand

- The full **Cotton Series**, from day pads to liners
- The new **Performance Series overnight pad**
- **Packaging options**, from retail boxes to recyclable wraps
- Samples you can take home and test

<PullQuote cite="Kawada sales team">
The best way to judge a pad is to hold it. Come and feel the difference between the two series.
</PullQuote>

## Book a meeting

Our sales and product teams will be on the stand all three days. Meetings are 30 minutes and cover your range, your timeline and your MOQ. Book ahead and we will have samples ready for your category.

## Can't make it?

We can send the same sample kit by courier, or set up a video call with the team. [Get in touch](/en/contact-us/) either way.

articles.title: A new overnight pad for our Performance Series
articles.excerpt: Longer coverage and a faster core, developed with partners for heavy-flow nights.
articles.coverAlt: Close-up of a Kawada pad absorbing liquid
articles.body:
Nights are where pads are tested hardest. Long hours, changing positions and heavy flow all at once. Our partners asked for an overnight pad that could keep up, so we built one for the Performance Series.

## What is new

- **Longer coverage** at the back, where most overnight leaks start
- **A faster core** that pulls fluid away from the surface quickly
- **Wider wings** that stay put when you move in your sleep
- **A soft, breathable backsheet** that stays quiet

<PullQuote cite="Kawada product team">
We tested it the way people actually sleep: on their side, on their back, and everything in between.
</PullQuote>

## Developed with partners

The design went through several rounds of samples with partner brands before it was finalised. Each round was tested in our lab for absorption, rewet and leakage, and the feedback shaped the shape, the length and the wing design.

<Figure
  src="/images/home/range-overnight-pad.jpg"
  alt="The overnight pad laid flat to show its length and wings"
  caption="Extra length at the back, where overnight leaks usually start."
/>

## Ready for your brand

The overnight pad is available now for OEM and private label, with your choice of length, packaging and print. See the full specs on the [product page](/en/products/feminine-400mm/), or [request samples](/en/contact-us/).

articles.title: Where our materials come from
articles.excerpt: From cotton field to topsheet. How we choose, trace and check the materials in every pad we make.
articles.coverAlt: Close-up of the soft absorbent fibres in a Kawada pad
articles.body:
A pad is only as good as what goes into it. The topsheet touches skin for hours, the core has to absorb fast, and the backsheet has to stay quiet and breathable. So we treat material sourcing as product design, not purchasing.

## The layers, and what we look for

Each layer of a pad does a different job, and each one has its own supplier standards.

- **Topsheet**: soft, skin-friendly and quick to let fluid through. Cotton for the Cotton Series, a performance non-woven for the Performance Series.
- **Acquisition layer**: spreads fluid so the core can do its work evenly.
- **Absorbent core**: holds fluid and locks it away from the surface.
- **Backsheet**: breathable and leak-proof.
- **Adhesive and release paper**: hold firmly and peel cleanly.

> Good materials are not the most expensive ones. They are the ones that behave the same way in every roll.

## Tracing every lot

Every roll and bale that arrives is logged with its supplier, lot number and certificate. Incoming materials are inspected before they reach a line, and lot numbers follow the material all the way to the finished batch. If a question ever comes up about a shipment, we can trace it back to the material lot.

<Figure
  src="/images/home/about-cotton.jpg"
  alt="Close-up of soft cotton fibre"
  caption="Cotton for the Cotton Series topsheet is traced lot by lot."
/>

## Choosing suppliers

We work with a short list of approved suppliers and audit them regularly. A new supplier has to pass sample testing, a trial production run and a full batch test before their material goes into a partner's product.

## Greener options

More partners are asking for plant-based and biodegradable materials. We test these to the same standard as everything else, so a greener pad never has to be a weaker one. [Talk to us](/en/contact-us/) about the options for your range.

articles.title: How we test every production batch
articles.excerpt: Weight, absorbency, leakage and adhesion. The checks every batch passes before it ships, and why we never skip one.
articles.coverAlt: Quality technicians checking a production batch in the Kawada cleanroom
articles.body:
When a brand puts its name on a pad we make, it is trusting us with its reputation. That trust is earned one batch at a time, so every batch is tested before it leaves the factory. No exceptions, no sampling holidays.

## What we test

Samples are pulled from the start, middle and end of each run. Each sample goes through the same set of checks:

- **Weight and dimensions**, to confirm the pad matches its spec sheet
- **Absorption speed and capacity**, using standard test fluid
- **Rewet**, to make sure the surface stays dry under pressure
- **Leakage**, on an inclined test bench
- **Adhesion**, so the pad stays in place and peels off cleanly
- **Packaging seal and print**, checked against the approved artwork

<PullQuote cite="Kawada quality team">
A batch that passes on Monday says nothing about Tuesday. That is why we test every one.
</PullQuote>

## What happens when a batch fails

If a sample falls outside spec, the batch is held. We trace the cause, whether that is a material lot, a machine setting or a packaging issue, fix it, and retest. A held batch only ships when it passes, and the partner sees the full record.

<Figure
  src="/images/home/factory-lab.jpg"
  alt="A technician weighing a pad sample on a lab balance"
  caption="Samples are pulled from the start, middle and end of every run."
/>

## Records you can see

Every batch gets a test report tied to its lot number. Partners can request the reports for any shipment, and we keep them on file so a question two years from now still has an answer.

## Why it matters for your brand

Consistent product means fewer complaints, fewer returns and fewer surprises for your customers. It also makes audits and retailer onboarding faster, because the evidence is already there.

Want to see a sample report? [Ask our team](/en/contact-us/) and we will send one over.

articles.title: Highlights from CIDPEX 2026
articles.excerpt: Three days, hundreds of conversations. What buyers asked us about at this year's disposable paper expo, and what it says about the market.
articles.body:
Thank you to everyone who visited our stand at CIDPEX this year. Here is what we heard most often, and what it tells us about where the market is going.

## Three questions we heard all week

1. **Can you do a cotton topsheet at our price point?** Cotton is no longer a niche request. Brands in every market asked about it.
2. **What are the greener options?** Plant-based and biodegradable materials came up in almost every conversation.
3. **How low can the MOQ go?** New brands want to test a range before committing to large runs.

<PullQuote cite="Kawada sales team">
The conversation has moved from "what does it cost" to "what is it made of".
</PullQuote>

## What we showed

We brought the Cotton Series, early samples of the Performance Series overnight pad and our packaging range. The overnight pad samples ran out on day two.

<Figure
  src="/images/home/series-cotton.jpg"
  alt="Cotton Series pads on display"
  caption="The Cotton Series drew the most questions on the stand."
/>

## What comes next

We are following up with every visitor who left their details. If we missed you, [get in touch](/en/contact-us/) and we will send the sample kit.
